passage:
Five a.m. That's the part nobody puts on posters. I'm Aditi, and Ishita, you asked why I stopped pinning the runner's photos and started pinning her schedule. I read that she trained through school exams and two failed trials before her first medal.
So I copied a habit, not the image. Three mornings a week I run before school, slowly, and I tick each day in a notebook. Some days I honestly hate it. Last week I skipped once and felt guilty, and then I went out the next morning anyway.
My cousin says I'm copying her. But I'm not trying to become her. I'm trying to become someone who turns up for my own goals. That's what her story gave me: fuel.

qa.q: How many mornings a week does Aditi run before school?
qa.a: Aditi runs three mornings a week before school.

qa.q: What does Aditi mean by saying "I'm not trying" to become the runner?
qa.a: Aditi wants the runner's habits, not the runner's image, so the admiration works as fuel for Aditi's own goals.

qa.q: What would you advise Aditi on a day the run feels hateful?
qa.a: Keep the routine small, tick the notebook, and remember that the runner's success came from years of discipline, including failed trials. 👍

qa.q: Why might Aditi's cousin see Aditi's running differently?
qa.a: The cousin may think Aditi is only imitating the athlete, without seeing that Aditi wants the discipline rather than the fame.

grounding: Shows a teen admiring an athlete's years of discipline and copying habits rather than image.

passage:

Nitin: the sprinter? ya
Joseph: 10 YEARS of training at 5am before anyone knew her name
Joseph: she ran on a mud track in her village with borrowed shoes
Nitin: ya that part got me
Joseph: i've been thinking. i always wanted to be like her but i meant like... the medal, the fame
Nitin: lol same
Joseph: but the real thing was the boring stuff. sleep early. warm up properly. write down every run
Nitin: so what, u're going to start running at 5?
Joseph: not 5. 6. but ya. every day. and i'll log it like she did
Nitin: can i join? i'm so slow tho
Joseph: she was slow once too apparently
Joseph: the medal part is her story. the habits can be mine
Nitin: ok deep 😄
Nitin: 6am at the ground. if i'm late throw a stone at my window
Joseph: deal 👍

qa.q: How many years did the sprinter train before anyone knew her name?
qa.a: She trained for 10 years at 5am before anyone knew her name.

qa.q: What does Joseph feel about the sprinter after the documentary?
qa.a: Joseph feels deep admiration and inspiration, especially for the years of quiet discipline behind her success.

qa.q: What did Joseph decide to copy from the sprinter, and why is it wise?
qa.a: Joseph decided to copy her habits, running daily and logging each run, instead of chasing the medal and fame, which gives Joseph something to actually do.

qa.q: How might Nitin feel about joining Joseph?
qa.a: Nitin seems excited but a little unsure about being slow, and is glad to have a friend to train with.

grounding: It shows a teen who admires an athlete for years of discipline, deciding to copy the habits rather than the image and using admiration as fuel.

passage:
Everyone in Sonipat knew about the wrestler from their district who had won at the national games. Suraj had her poster above his bed and watched every interview.

"I'm getting the same haircut," his friend Vikas announced on the way to the akhada. "And those gold shoes she wears."

Suraj laughed. But that night he watched her interview again, the part nobody shared. She talked about waking at four every day for eight years, about her coach making her repeat one move a thousand times, about crying after losses and coming back the next morning anyway.

The next day at the akhada, Suraj asked the coach, "Can I stay after for extra practice on the leg hold?"

"Why the leg hold?"

"She said she practised one move until it was boring. I want to do that."

The coach looked at him for a moment. "Good. Thirty minutes. Every day."

Vikas got the haircut. Suraj got blisters. Both of them grinned about it.

qa.q: What did Vikas want to copy from the wrestler?
qa.a: Vikas wanted the same haircut and her gold shoes.

qa.q: What was Suraj feeling as he watched the interview again?
qa.a: Suraj felt inspired and admiring, moved by the years of early mornings and the hard work behind her win.

qa.q: What did Suraj choose to copy, and why was that wise?
qa.a: Suraj chose to copy her habit of practising one move again and again, which builds real skill instead of just copying her look.

qa.q: How might the coach see Suraj's request?
qa.a: The coach seems pleased and impressed that Suraj wants to do the dull, repeated work that actually makes a wrestler better.

grounding: It shows a teen who admires an athlete for the discipline behind her success, copying her habits rather than her image and using admiration as fuel.
